title: A Monsoon for the Escarpment
premise: Ulyana Marchetti has spent a decade running cargo up the Verrane River, outrunning debts, memories, and the inheritance she refuses to claim from the family that disowned her. When dying prospector Elias Thorn trades her his map to a lost concession claim in exchange for a promise to deliver it before the permits expire, she inherits not wealth but a target on her hull. Hunted by the mining syndicate's enforcer and shadowed by Nadia, a surveyor with her own claim to the truth, Ulyana must navigate the monsoon-swollen river in a leaking boat, choosing between the safe life of perpetual motion and the dangerous weight of staying. In the end, she delivers the map, exposes the syndicate's forged permits, and claims both the escarpment claim and the family name she once abandoned.
about_author: Yara Dunmore is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years charting seasonal rivers across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels from a houseboat that migrates with the flood season.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Ulyana pilots her aging riverboat, the Kestrel, through low-water season, establishing her rule: never stop moving. A port official hints someone is asking about her family name. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: restless competence masking old wounds.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elias Thorn, feverish and half-drowned, stumbles aboard at a fueling dock and offers Ulyana a hand-drawn map to an unregistered concession claim on the Escarpment plateau — if she swears to file it before the permits lapse in thirty days. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Thorn dies at dawn; syndicate men arrive asking questions. Ulyana finds the map sewn into his coat and realizes she's already implicated. She casts off early with an unexpected passenger: Nadia Reyes, a surveyor who claims Thorn was her mentor. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Passenger with Her Own Compass
chapters.summary: Nadia proves useful reading currents but evasive about why the syndicate wants her too. Ulyana tests her loyalty with a detour through smuggler channels; Nadia passes, barely. POV: alternating Ulyana/Nadia. Emotional beat: wary mutual respect kindling attraction.

chapters.title: The Enforcer's Wake
chapters.summary: Syndicate enforcer Corvo Halstead boards at a trading post, polite and lethal, offering to buy the map. Ulyana lies smoothly for the first time in years and hates how good it feels. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the thrill and shame of deception.

chapters.title: Clouds Over the Concession
chapters.summary: Radio reports confirm monsoon season arriving weeks early. The river will rise violently — faster travel, but deadly water and closed checkpoints. They must ride the storm or lose the window. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: dread reframed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Leaking at Kilometer Forty
chapters.summary: An old collision scar splits open in rising water; the Kestrel takes on bilge faster than the pump handles. They beach on a sandbar to patch her as the first storm cells build on the horizon. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: vulnerability — the boat is her armor cracking.

chapters.title: Nadia's Confession
chapters.summary: Patching seams by lamplight, Nadia admits Thorn forged her survey credentials years ago; the syndicate holds that over her, which is why they're hunting her. Ulyana must decide whether loyalty or truth governs this partnership. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: confession met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The First Monsoon Night
chapters.summary: The storm hits in full force. They run the flooded gorge by lightning-flash navigation, nearly losing the boat against a submerged tree. Ulyana saves them with a maneuver only she knows. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce joy.

chapters.title: Checkpoint of Broken Promises
chapters.summary: A flooded checkpoint forces them ashore, where Ulyana discovers the syndicate has already filed a competing claim using forged documents — and her estranged brother Marco signed as their attorney. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: betrayal reopening the oldest wound.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Trapped by weather in a river town, Ulyana finally tells Nadia about the Marchetti inheritance she walked away from — land, name, and a father who chose the syndicate's money over her. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: Marco at the Landing
chapters.summary: Marco intercepts them, ostensibly to warn Ulyana, actually to retrieve the map. He reveals the permits expire in nine days and the syndicate knows their route. He leaves an ultimatum instead of a warning. POV: Marco (brief) then Ulyana. Emotional beat: love and duty colliding within one family.

chapters.title: Running the Flooded Narrows
chapters.summary: They take the illegal high-water channel locals call the Throat — the only route that beats Corvo to the registry office. The Kestrel's engine floods; they drift the worst rapid engineless. POV: Nadia. Emotional bet: trust fully extended and answered.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Become Crew
chapters.summary: River families who owe Ulyana quiet favors shelter and repair the boat overnight, feeding them and lying to Corvo's scouts. Ulyana realizes she has built a life worth defending after all. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: belonging discovered where she least expected it.

chapters.title: Corvo Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Corvo seizes the registry office road and sends word: surrender the map or he burns the Kestrel at anchor. Nadia proposes a gambit — deliver a decoy map while filing the real claim by radio relay through a surveyor friend. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: courage borrowed from love.

chapters.title: The Decoy Run
chapters.summary: Ulyana hands Corvo a convincing forgery and watches him sail triumphantly toward coordinates that don't exist. Guilt wars with relief; she has become everything she despised in her father. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: moral cost of survival.

chapters.title: Escarpment Rising
chapters.summary: They reach the Escarpment base as the monsoon peaks. Climbing to verify the claim markers, Nadia and Ulyana find evidence the syndicate's original permit was fraudulent all along — Thorn had proof. POV: Nadia. Emotional beat: truth as weapon and burden.

chapters.title: The Permit Clock
chapters.summary: With hours left, the radio relay fails mid-transmission. The only way to file is physically reaching the district office upriver — directly past Corvo, who has discovered the decoy. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cornered clarity.

chapters.title: All Water Is One Water
chapters.summary: Climax: Ulyana runs the Kestrel straight through Corvo's blockade in peak flood, ramming past his launch in a ferocious set piece. Marco, witnessing Corvo's brutality, turns and testifies to the forged permits. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: every theme converging in one reckless act of faith.

chapters.title: Filed Before the Rain Ends
chapters.summary: They reach the district office soaked and bleeding; the clerk stamps the claim minutes before the permits lapse. Corvo is arrested on Marco's testimony. Ulyana stands in the rain holding paper that means roots. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: exhaustion and disbelief becoming hope.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: Ulyana visits her father's grave for the first time, reads his unsent letter, and chooses to reclaim the Marchetti name — on her terms, with Nadia beside her. Marco asks forgiveness; she offers time, not absolution. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: A Boat Worth Anchoring
chapters.summary: Epilogue: the Kestrel repaired, the escarpment claim surveyed honestly under both their names, Ulyana moors the boat for a full season for the first time in a decade. Stopping no longer costs more than moving. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: stillness chosen, not imposed — love as harbor.
